canonical_statement: The authors report a post-neurosurgical carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae meningitis case treated with ceftazidime/avibactam plus intraventricular gentamicin.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We report a case of post-neurosurgical meningitis

canonical_statement: The reported patient was elderly and presented with acute headache and loss of consciousness, diffuse subarachnoid and intraventricular hemorrhage, early obstructive hydrocephalus, and required an external ventricular drain.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: An elderly patient presented with acute-onset headache and loss of consciousness

population.label: Single elderly post-neurosurgical patient with carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae meningitis

canonical_statement: The BAL and CSF K. pneumoniae isolates were screened as carbapenemase producers with CARBA NP as part of the laboratory workflow.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Both isolates were carbapenemase producers determined by CARBA NP

canonical_statement: Table 1 reports MIC susceptibility testing by an automated broth-microdilution platform; ceftazidime/avibactam and polymyxin B susceptibility were determined by Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Susceptibilities and MICs determined by an automated platform using broth microdilution.

canonical_statement: For the CRE meningitis episode, ceftazidime/avibactam was restarted, intraventricular gentamicin 8 mg daily was initiated, and the EVD was exchanged the following day.

canonical_statement: The authors present successful use of ceftazidime/avibactam plus intraventricular gentamicin for CRE meningitis and call for additional clinical and pharmacokinetic studies.
